summary: This review article comprehensively covers coherent control of population and quantum coherence in superconducting quantum circuits (SQCs), progressing from field quantization through the Jaynes-Cummings model to multilevel phenomena in circuit QED. The work demonstrates how dressed-state engineering enables quantum-optical effects such as electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT), Autler-Townes splitting (ATS), and stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) in superconducting artificial atoms coupled to microwave resonators.
motivation: Superconducting circuits offer a macroscopic platform for exploring quantum coherence and control beyond natural atomic systems, with advantages including strong light-matter coupling ($g/2\pi \approx 1$-$100$ MHz), engineered energy spectra via external parameters, and easy integration into quantum processors.
method: The review develops quantization of electromagnetic fields in cavity modes and lumped LC circuits, introduces the Lindblad master equation for open quantum systems, discusses transmon and flux qubit implementations with anharmonicity $E_C/\hbar \approx 100$-$500$ MHz, and describes engineering of three-level $\Lambda$ systems in doubly-dressed polariton states via external microwave drives at controlled detunings $\Delta/2\pi$.
result: Key demonstrations include EIT with probe absorption suppression via coherent control when $\Omega_c < (\Gamma_{31} - \gamma_{21})/2$, ATS-induced spectral splitting proportional to control Rabi frequency $\Omega_c$, and accelerated population transfer via superadiabatic STIRAP (saSTIRAP) that bypasses strict adiabatic constraints while maintaining high fidelity coherent control without populating intermediate states.
